messages:
Anya: quick q — we're seeing a weird combo where route-level flag 'enable_rerank' is true but model-level override sets it false for the rerank model. which one should win?
Mike: by current doc, more specific scope wins (model > route > project > org), so model override should win. did you hit a regression?
Anya: yeah small one in search canary. rerank off at model causes low quality for a subset of users. the canary route expected route-level true to take effect.
Sylvie: hmm that sounds like the intended behavior is route to control routing behavior. we need to confirm precedence for 'behavioral' flags vs 'model' flags.
Charles: we discussed a split last quarter: config flags that change model inference should let model-level overrides win, but route-level rollout flags intended for traffic gating should be higher precedence. not codified though.
Anya: ok so ambiguity is the problem. can we add a quick lint that flags mixed-scope definitions for the same flag key?
Mike: +1. we have a small PR that adds scope validation in the flag service. I can bump it up. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/flag-service/pull/412
Sylvie: maybe the rule: if flag annotated with @cross-scope: true then route takes precedence, else model wins. simple annotation.
Charles: I like annotation. avoids changing lots of existing flags. but need to handle canary audiences too — e.g., route canary audience should be honored even if model-level value differs for non-canary users.
Anya: example: route A has canary audience 10% where enable_rerank=true. model M has override false for everyone. for the 10% we *do* want rerank on. so route canary should be applied first for that audience.
FlagBot: automated note — flag key 'enable_rerank' has two active overrides: model:M:false (created 2169900000 by Charles) and route:A:true (created 2170005000 by Anya).
Mike: proposal: precedence algorithm: 1) per-request audience check -> if route canary matches, use route override; 2) else use most-specific non-audience override (model > route > project > org) with annotation exceptions.
Sylvie: sounds good. can we get an ops guardrail to prevent model-level overrides from turning off a flag for routes that have active canaries? alert on config push if it would break an active canary.
Charles: yep we can add a preflight check in the flag CI that scans active canaries and rejects model override pushes that reduce feature coverage for them.
Anya: perfect. can someone add a short note in the rollout playbook and ping product? I can file a tiny doc change.
Mike: I'll update the flag-service PR to include the audience-first precedence and add a lint rule.
Sylvie: tagging @product for sync: product please confirm annotation approach acceptable for policy.
Anya: thanks — will follow up once PR merges. :thumbsup:
